card.title: One-Act Play 2 — A Sunny Morning (Serafín and Joaquín Álvarez Quintero)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The play at a glance "A Sunny Morning" by Serafín and Joaquín Álvarez Quintero is a one-act romantic comedy set in a Madrid park on an autumn morning. Don Gonzalo, a crotchety old gentleman, and Doña Laura, a sharp-tongued old lady, collide over a park bench — and discover, through a web of polite lies, that they were lovers decades ago.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Former lovers meet as old strangers — neither recognises the other at first.
Humour comes from vanity: both invent glamorous versions of their past.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: The crumbs and the bench: small props carry nostalgia — link one prop to the theme of lost love and time.  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **Doña Laura** is wit wrapped in white hair: sharp-tongued, vain, quick to fence and quicker to fall — her anger at the bench softens the moment the snuffbox appears, and her lies are more elaborate than his because she has more to protect (the "Silver Maiden" was a reputation as well as a romance).…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **Love outlasting time** — the central theme: the lovers' recognition survives fifty years, disguises and mutual lies; the doves and the snuffbox prove memory is stronger than ageing. **Vanity and dignity in old age** — the lies are comic but human: neither wants to be seen as diminished, so each invents a glorious version of the other's past.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. How do Don Gonzalo and Doña Laura first meet? (2 marks)** A. In conflict over a park bench: he grumbles that the pigeons ate his crumbs and the priests took his seat, and finds her installed where he usually sits. Their exchange of polite insults is comic warfare that turns, by way of a dropped snuffbox, into recognition. **Q.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. How do Dona Laura and Don Gonzalo conceal their identities at first? (2 marks) — each invents a younger self and a fictional past, afraid of ridicule.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "The play is a comedy of recognition." Trace the steps by which the old couple discover each other. (8 marks)** A model answer maps the arc: the bench quarrel (courtship in the grammar of insult), the truce over the snuffbox (the physical token of the past), the coded exchange about the Silver Maiden and the gallant young man (each testing the other's memory), the confirming details…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The action, scene by scene The play opens on comedy of manners: Don Gonzalo enters grumbling — the pigeons ate his breadcrumbs, the priests took his bench — and finds Doña Laura installed on his usual seat. Their first exchanges are comic warfare: she calls him a "senile grouch"; he retaliates with courtesy sharpened into insult; she reads her book with "magnificent" disdain.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Dramatic irony** — the play's engine: the audience watches two people lie to each other about the one thing they both know, and every "as a gardener I have no education" lands twice — once for the listener on stage, once for the audience in on the truth.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: The play's charm is RECOGNITION: two elderly ex-sweeteners meet as strangers feeding birds and gradually recognise each other — the gradual reveal structure is the answer.  ·  Trick 2: Vanity and age: each pretends to be younger and blames the other for not recognising them — the comic irony of mutual self-deception.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What is the theme of the play? (2 marks) — ageing, vanity and the sweet persistence of first love.
